cards.b: Biologist Theodosius Dobzhansky said nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution. Why antibiotics stop working, why we have an appendix and why a crow looks like a crow all follow from one simple idea.

Evolution is change in the inherited traits of populations over generations. Charles Darwin spent five years (1831-36) on HMS Beagle. Alfred Russel Wallace reached the same idea independently; both presented it in 1858. Darwin's book On the Origin of Species came out in 1859.

1. Variation: individuals differ.
  2. Inheritance: traits pass to offspring.
  3. Overproduction: more are born than survive.
  4. Differential success: those with helpful traits leave more offspring.

The peppered moth in industrial England: before 1850 most were pale and hid on lichen. Soot darkened trees, and dark moths survived better. By 1895 dark ones dominated in Manchester. After clean air laws, pale ones returned. Bernard Kettlewell's 1950s experiments tested this.
'Fitness' means reproductive success, not strength. An adaptation is a trait shaped by selection. Selection acts on individuals, but populations evolve.

Besides selection: mutation (new variants), genetic drift (chance changes, strong in small groups), gene flow (migration) and sexual selection (mate choice, like peacock tails). Hardy-Weinberg (1908) is the baseline for no change.

Lamarck (1809) proposed that traits acquired in life are inherited, such as a giraffe stretching its neck. This is wrong. Malthus (1798) on population pressure inspired Darwin. Mendel's genetics, joined with Darwin in the 1930s-40s, formed the modern synthesis. Darwin's finches in the Galapagos show beak shape tracking food: Peter and Rosemary Grant measured it over decades.

Fix these

  • Evolution is not 'survival of the strongest'; it is survival and reproduction of the fit for a place.
  • Individuals do not evolve; populations do.
  • Evolution has no goal or progress ladder.
  • 'Theory' in science means a well-tested explanation.

Antibiotic resistance in Indian hospitals, including NDM-1 (named for New Delhi), is selection in action. Biodiversity hotspots like the Western Ghats hold many unique species formed by long isolation. J.B.S. Haldane, who moved to India in 1957, helped found modern population genetics and worked at the Indian Statistical Institute.

• Variation + inheritance + overproduction + differential success.
  • Darwin and Wallace, 1858; Origin, 1859.
  • Drift, mutation, gene flow also drive change.

Think about it:

  1. How would Lamarck and Darwin each explain the giraffe's neck?
  2. Why does overusing antibiotics speed up resistance?

quiz.q: Who studied finches' beaks over decades?
